Address a code review of PR #527 (change 325, branch `fix/degraded-results-are-not-kept`, head 03589371, trail 469) in the caliper repo. In your worktree: `git fetch origin`, `git switch -c fix-527f origin/fix/degraded-results-are-not-kept`; push with `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/fix/degraded-results-are-not-kept` (normal fast-forward; NEVER force). You OWN crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs, crates/core/src/dependency_types/** (ledger.rs is the heart), crates/core/src/pipeline/revision/lazy.rs, crates/core/src/pipeline/revision.rs, crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs, crates/core/src/pipeline/tests.rs, crates/semantic/src/kept.rs, instantiate.rs, declared.rs, lib.rs (comment edits only there), and `.changeset/degraded-results-are-not-kept.md`; touch nothing else. Read first: /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/worker-contract.md, evidence-types-direction.md and diagnose-after-three-findings.md, AGENTS.md ('Writing and commits': comments only the non-obvious why, no history; changesets: one idea per bullet, written for users), CONTRIBUTING.md, `gh pr view 527`, /tmp/claude-501/pr-degraded.md (rounds 1-7: `ReadLedger`, provisional answer footprint, `Settled::Degraded` + `DEGRADED_RETRY`). Rules: signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/ (own gate fixture: `node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs /tmp/claude-501/fix527f/gate-large`); update the PR body FILE /tmp/claude-501/pr-degraded.md in place ('Round 8'); I publish the body and resolve findings. Final message max 170 words: head SHA, per item CONFIRMED (failing test)/refuted/dismissed, blockers. Cap 130 tool calls; never ask questions. Verify each real item with a failing test on 03589371 first; fix the class and grep siblings.

THE REVIEW: (1) A failed read recorded by a `Retry::Always` load is stamped with `edits = 0` (ledger.rs ~109: `(Instant::now(), 0, 0)`); a lazy session compares that to its real edit count, so after any edit the walk reads as due on EVERY request (a load and a resolution per request, no 30 s backoff): UNCONFIRMED by the reviewer: trace whether a lazy session can inherit a layer from an `Always` load (cold/eager load, flatten); if so, stamp reads with the session's CURRENT edit count at record time (or make the stamp a typed `Edits` taken from the load's context, never a literal 0); test: eager/cold load fails a read, then a lazy session that has already seen N edits requests it repeatedly: at most one retry inside the backoff. (2) `Settled::Stopped` (the checker stopped mid-request: delivery None) is neither kept nor held as a refusal: the settle match has no arm for it, so a crash-looping checker is asked again by EVERY request/prefetch/story load, which the doc comments say must not happen (semantic_hook.rs ~360): hold it like `Degraded` for the backoff (explicit marker, not cached as an answer, not stored), keep `awaits_checker` semantics, injectable clock; test: a fake provider that stops: N requests inside the window send one request; after the window it asks again; a recovered checker's answer replaces it; sibling-sweep every `Settled`/`Found` variant for the same 'no arm' hole: make the match exhaustive with NO wildcard so a new variant cannot be forgotten. (3) PERF (wall time first): every lazy growth rebuilds the whole unread-walk reverse graph (`layer.unread_walks()` builds `latest` and `reached_by` over every mark in the chain) and scans every project file's demands (lazy.rs ~679): cache the `UnreadWalks` per layer (computed once per layer, invalidated when a layer is added) and do the demand scan only for demands that can reach an unread walk; counter test: M growths on a chain with one unreadable file build the graph once per layer; report instructions retired (`/usr/bin/time -l`) before/after on a Chakra lazy/watch scenario if the harness exists (else the counter only). (4) The 30 s interval is defined twice (`READ_RETRY` in ledger.rs, `DEGRADED_RETRY` in semantic_hook.rs), kept equal by a doc comment: one shared constant in one place both import (core crate, e.g. a `retry` module or in types), with a compile-level link; test that both sides use it. (5) `Footprint` wraps an anonymous 4-tuple `(PathKey, u64, Instant, u64)` so load/edits are positionally interchangeable: replace with a named struct (path, load, at, edits) or hold the failed read's identity directly; typed newtypes for `Load` and `Edits` so a transposition does not compile. (6) Comments describing history violate AGENTS.md ('only the non-obvious why, no history'): cut every 'On the base ...' / 'before this change' / 'was previously' comment and doc across the whole PR diff (`git diff origin/main...HEAD` and grep) in kept.rs, declared.rs, lib.rs, instantiate.rs, lazy.rs, pipeline/tests.rs and everywhere else you own, re-filling each touched block to 120 columns; do NOT touch files you do not own (list any you found). (7) `partial_exports` (dependency_types.rs ~401) is only ever added to across layers and flattens: a later load that follows the demand again but finds only an incomplete `None` leaves the older layer's partial mapping standing, so `export_for_resolver` falls back through `chain().find_map(partial_exports)` to a stale mapping (e.g. the file becomes readable and declares the name, or the barrel was edited): the NEWEST walk of that demand must supersede: store the newest walk's partial mapping per (barrel, name) with its generation and have the newest layer's outcome (including 'nothing found') win; test: partial found, then file readable and declares Name itself: the resolver gets the new declaration; barrel edited: stale mapping gone; and add it to the model test. (8) `BatchAnswers` memory/serialization (asked.rs): DISMISS in the body (on main already via #513, a measured Chakra memory gate shows no regression, follow-up). (9) `.changeset/degraded-results-are-not-kept.md`: rewrite per the repo rules: one idea per bullet, users' words, no internals (no 'provisional answers', 'loads', 'resolutions'), the 'What you see now' bullet split into single-idea bullets, repeated bullets merged; keep the `**Breaking:**` paragraph for the public fields if present. Verify: mantine/chakra output identical to origin/main (drop SEMANTIC_BACKEND non-info runs by code and severity), `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (pty/watch tests need the sandbox off), `just test-checker-lane` (outside the sandbox, no CARGO_TARGET_DIR), `gate_harness determinism` and `memory --tsc built-in` on your own fixture, and tests/session_equals_cold.rs from `origin/test/session-equals-cold` run against your tree (do not commit it). Mutation-prove each new rule.

name: worker-contract
description: "Rules every caliper worker follows (scope, branch/push, targeted checks, call cap, PR body, pre-push gate). Copied from the deleted caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md on 2026-11-17; paths to fixtures no longer exist"

  type: reference

  modified: 2026-11-18T01:13:52.369Z
---

Restored from my reading of `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/worker-contract.md` (deleted by the user 2026-11-17; see [[fixtures-is-not-scratch]]). Changes made while restoring: no build output or scratch in `caliper-fixtures`; PR bodies go in `$TMPDIR` or the worktree, not there.

**Scope**: edit only the files the brief names; if another must change, stop and say which and why. Never ask the user questions; if blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work.

**Branch and push**: branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Build in the worktree's own `target/` (the `just test-checker-lane` recipe hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`). Plain `rustc` is 1.99.1 here; the old note about the mise shim forcing 1.98.1 did not reproduce on 2026-11-17. Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: <session url>`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, fully qualified when pushing a bare SHA), never `--no-verify`, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Workers do not open or edit the PR and do not poll CI.

**Checks, targeted (CI runs the rest)**: always before push `just lint doc-check machete typos`. Then only what the change touches: Rust -> nextest of touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once (run it without a CARGO_TARGET_DIR override); checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` against a build of origin/main on a large fixture and a Chakra-only fixture. Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless that area changed. Tests must fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one. No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, prefer allocation or instruction counts.

**Cap**: stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what is verified; "not done, because X" beats burning calls.

**Artifacts**: PR body with `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line the session url; the lead publishes it unedited. Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers.

**Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new)**:
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms; everything else is Unknown/Declined (never "complete", "none", "exact"). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).
- Grammar sweep: list every syntax/type form the code can receive and show each is handled or declined (exhaustive match, or a generated test over the grammar with the checker/TS API as oracle). Generate over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Mutation proof: remove each guard/dependency; a test must fail. Report which you tried (cargo mutants --in-diff works).
- Before reporting: run `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then try to break your own change with inputs the diff did not mention (computed keys, symbols, getters, overloads, re-exports, shadowing, optional chains, declare/abstract, conditional types, lone surrogates).

name: evidence-types-direction
description: "2026-11-24 audits: findings share one root (verdicts from spelling, absence or degraded results); direction is evidence types, one owner per decision, architecture tests; reports in docs/audits/"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6f993b0f-3007-4088-bd26-63eda356278e
  modified: 2026-11-24T18:36:58.192Z
---

Three read-only audits on 2026-11-24 (reports committed on branch `docs/review-checklist` under `docs/audits/2026-11-24-*.md`) found that our recurring review findings are one root problem in three places: a DECISION is made from something that is not evidence. Extractor: a spelling (PascalCase callee, name lists, `contains("Component")`) or a raw expression. Wire boundary (crates/semantic): an ABSENT or defaulted field read as a value (`#[serde(default)]`, `unwrap_or(false)`, tsrs omits empty fields). Caches and sessions: a DEGRADED result (timeout, read failure, heap budget, nesting cut) stored as authoritative. The rules already exist in prose (CONTRIBUTING 'Before you push', ADR 0025-0028: by binding not spelling, one owner per decision, unknown unless proven, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading); nothing enforces them in code.

**Why:** reviews found 3 + 3 + 5 findings per PR in the same classes; each fix moved the problem (validating on a shared cache primed it the other way). Fixing per site does not converge.

**How to apply (direction, in this order):** (1) failing-first counter-example suites (extractor M10: every snippet in the audit becomes a row asserting exact output); (2) make invalid states unrepresentable: `ComponentEvidence` required to build a `ComponentMapping`, a typed `Peeled` (Transparent | Instantiated | Asserted) with one exhaustive match, `Known<T>` for decoded wire fields, a `Degraded` marker on outcomes that no cache or kept answer stores, `CallError::Contract` for undecodable responses with its own code; (3) one owner modules (`extractor/decide.rs`, `semantic/src/wire.rs` with one tsrs version-pin test, one `Memo` abstraction); (4) architecture tests (grep-based Rust tests, no new scripts) that fail on a catch-all arm or a name literal in a decision, `unwrap_or(false)` on wire values, text matching of messages, statics in non-test code; (5) determinism as a tested property: differential tests with separate state per consumer as oracle, session equals cold extract under random edit scripts. Amend ADR 0027/0026: 'a name is a candidate filter, never a verdict'. Related: [[diagnose-after-three-findings]], [[workers-run-full-lint-gate]].

name: diagnose-after-three-findings
description: "After three findings on one PR stop routing spot fixes: tabulate them, name root causes (one decision with two owners, state keyed wrong, singletons), decide if the design must change"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ad4b3461-bb6f-49f0-bb4d-997d9b8887ba
  modified: 2026-11-16T01:05:54.318Z
---

On 2026-11-14 the user said they were "disappointed that you're not taking a step back to understand the patterns, consider the architecture and our models" after the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462) collected 11 findings over 5 rounds that I routed one at a time as spot fixes. I had promised a model-based approach "if another finding appears" and still patched the next one.

**Why:** findings arrive serially from a reviewer that sees a slice each round; workers capped at 25-35 calls patch the symptom. The 11 findings shared four root causes: no explicit lifecycle model (state scattered across flags keyed by the wrong dimension: component instead of component+revision+key+client), decisions made in two places (lazy vs eager, structural vs checker diagnostics, two dev servers), last-writer-wins singletons where truth is a per-client set, and TypeScript re-deriving what the Rust core already owns. Same smell as #455 (two walkers decide eligibility), #459 (two paths feed the kept answer), #458.

**How to apply:**
- Third finding on a PR: stop; make a table of the findings, name the root causes, ask 'is one decision made or held in two places?' and 'what is the state machine and who owns it?'.
- Remedy shape: one owner for each decision (prefer the Rust core's merged answer over re-deriving in TS), one explicit reducer (pure state x event -> state x effects), and a model-based/property test of the invariants after quiescence, with the earlier findings as named regression sequences.
- Give such a worker room (cap ~100 calls, Opus); caps suit mechanical work, not stateful mechanisms.
- Before accepting any worker fix ask: is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?

**Second instance, 2026-11-15 (#467, tsrs_module swapped for oxc_resolver):** five findings in five rounds, each in glue code that re-created an old behaviour (symlink canonicalization, `.cts` conditions, relative tsconfig, fingerprint inputs, a `baseUrl` fallback that guessed which rule answered from whether the path contained `node_modules`). I called the root cause settled twice and was wrong twice. The user: "How are you not guarding against these coming up???"

**Why:** a behaviour-preserving library swap was gated by a single-run identity diff on two fixtures, which cannot see cross-run cache staleness or inputs the fixtures lack; fix rounds added new heuristic code that nothing exercised; the Entire reviewer was the first real review. The swap's premise ("same results, less code") was false: tsrs follows TypeScript 7 (no `baseUrl` for bare specifiers) where the old resolver followed TypeScript 6, and the PR grew to +768/-222.

**How to apply:**
- Before a swap: inventory every behaviour of the replaced component that the code relies on (options, conditions, symlinks, config inheritance, cache keys) and diff old against new over the cross-product, not two fixtures.
- Before pushing any worker branch: read the diff myself for heuristics (a rule inferred from path shape, a guess) and run `/code-review` on it; do not let the Entire reviewer be the first review.
- At the third finding re-test the premise (does the swap still delete more than it adds?), not only the root cause; if not, close the PR.

**Third instance, 2026-11-15 (about 50 findings across trails 404/405):** the user said "consider all of the findings together, architecturally and semantically ... make sure the agents won't find even more things". Eight root classes (silence read as evidence, lossy model asserting exactness, spelling instead of binding, derived state outside the dependency model, one decision with two owners, host assumptions, hand-tuned policy with no reference model, contract drift / fields never populated). Table: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md.

**Why:** guards were DENY-lists (enumerate the wrong cases found so far), so each new grammar form (a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) produced the next finding; about 40% of the raw count was the same code repeated in stacked child PRs.

**How to apply:**
- Design guards as ALLOW-lists: a closed set of proven forms, everything else Unknown/Declined; exhaustive matches, no wildcard arms in decisions.
- Run the pre-push gate in worker-contract.md (invariants, grammar sweep with the checker/TS API as oracle, mutation proof, adversarial pass, then /code-review) before any push; generate tests over the grammar, not over past findings.
- Merge stacks in order and retarget children; do not keep a stack alive across review rounds.

See [[resolve-findings-when-fixed]] and [[worker-token-budget]].

## What

Two shared-state defects where a transient failure was stored as an answer. Both confirmed by tests that fail on `origin/main` (`f4a88f93`).

**1. A checker outage was kept as the component's answer** (`crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`; audit shared-state hit 1, semantic-wire hit 1).

- Cause: `read_outcome` turned an outcome with no component and no fallback (`SemanticOutcome::unavailable`: timeout, crash, checker not running) into `Answered { component: None, diagnostics: [] }`, and `ask` inserted every `Answered` into `cache.answers`. The warning went to a once-per-session `warned` flag. Every later request until a source edit got structural props, no diagnostic, `awaits_checker` false.
- Fix: the notion is a type. `Settled` gains `Degraded(Vec<Diagnostic>)`; `read_outcome` returns it for an outcome that answers nothing. `ask` inserts only `Settled::Answered`. `refine` attaches a degraded request's diagnostics (each with `affects` = the component) to every answer it affects. The `warned` flag is gone. The next request asks the checker again.
- `awaits_checker` stays false on a degraded answer: a checker that stays down (`MAX_RESTARTS`, could not start) answers at once, so a host that re-asked on `awaits_checker` would loop. Not caching is what makes the next request ask again.

**2. A failed dependency read was persisted as "not exported"** (`crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`; audit shared-state hit 4).

- Cause: `Loader::read` returned `None` on an I/O error, the `parsed` `OnceLock` stored `None`, `find_export_uncached` returned `None` without `cut`, the miss was cached, `learn`ed and written by `write_index` as `(module, name, None)`. Later runs trusted it while `package.json` was unchanged.
- Fix:
  - `read_text` returns `Err(Unreadable)` for a file that exists but cannot be read (still reports the Warning diagnostic once, as before). `parse_source` returns `Result<Option<_>, Unreadable>` and does not initialize the `parsed` cell on a failed read, so the next caller reads again.
  - `find_export_uncached` treats `Unreadable` as a cut (the cycle-cut mechanism): the miss is returned but neither kept, `learn`ed nor persisted.
  - The layer keeps only initialized `parsed` cells (`load`), so a session's next revision reads the file again instead of finding `None` in its parent.
  - `write_index` writes nothing when any dependency read failed in the run: an augmentation search's answer can hold the failure as an absence.

## Round 6

Review of `04bc55cd`: five fixes, four dismissals. Each fix has a test that fails with its rule removed (mutation list below).

**(a) Deciding a retry read the disk on every request** (`dependency_types/ledger.rs`). CONFIRMED by inspection: `FailedRead::is_due` called `std::fs::metadata` for each suspect file of each unread demand, inside `missing_at` and `unread`, on every request and every loop of `lazy_resolved`.

- Fix: the stamp is gone, so deciding a retry reads nothing from disk. A walk is due once `READ_RETRY` passed since its failure, an edit arrived (the edit count moved), or another walk read one of its files since. Checking the stamp only after the timer or an edit, as suggested, would add nothing: the walk is already due at that point. No `std::fs` call is left in `ledger.rs`. The zero-stat property holds by construction, and the request path is now a provisional memo hit (c): 0 loads, 0 resolutions, no ledger query beyond `unread_until`.
- Behaviour change, stated: a dependency file fixed on disk (an `npm install`, a `chmod`) is picked up at the retry (30 s) or the next source edit, not at once. The changeset says so. Four tests relied on the old immediate pickup. `ledger::tests` D (`a_prop_a_package_file_inherits_..._once_the_file_reads`), `Tag` and the model test, and `pipeline::tests::a_component_asked_while_a_dependency_file_could_not_be_read_is_answered_in_full_once_it_reads` (`pipeline/tests.rs`, outside the owned files, 4 lines) now make an edit after the file reads, which is the event that makes the walk due.

**(b) Every failed read of a load was a suspect of every unread walk in it** (`ledger.rs`, `dependency_types.rs`). CONFIRMED: `only_the_walk_whose_own_file_was_read_since_is_followed_again`. `A` and `B` are followed in one load, each behind its own unreadable file. A third component's walk reads `B`'s file again. With round 5's suspects `A` was walked again (cost `(1, 1)`, not `(0, 0)`); mutation R1 restores it.

- Fix: `ReadFailed` carries its path, and `Partial` carries `unread: Vec<PathKey>`, the files that walk could not read, in place of `incomplete: bool`. Every consumer over many files collects them: the export walk (`Unkept::unread`), the cause search, augmentation search, module demand, `load_declaration` and the React path. `unread_demand(demand, files)` records them, and a demand's mark holds exactly its own walk's files as `suspects`.

**(c) A component behind an unread walk was resolved again on every request** (`pipeline/revision/lazy.rs`). CONFIRMED: `read_retry_tests` requests inside the window cost `(0, 1)` before, `(0, 0)` now.

- Fix: `Lazy::provisional` holds the answer with the unread walks it reached. It answers while `DependencyLayer::unread_until(walks, edits)` is in the future: the earliest retry among the walks' own files. It is dropped once one of them is due, followed again by a later load, or has a file read since. It is not carried by `next_lazy` (an edit drops it), never enters `memo` and is never persisted.
- Tests (injectable clock): 5 requests inside the window `(0, 0)`; at retry - 1 ms `(0, 0)`; at the retry `(1, 1)`, then `(0, 0)` again; readable before the retry `(0, 0)`; after the retry `(1, 1)`, the answer equals a cold run's and is memoized `(0, 0)`. `an_edit_makes_the_walk_past_an_unreadable_file_due_at_once`: after an edit `(1, 1)`, equal to cold. The model test now asserts that a request made while every file reads, after an edit since the last file change, warns about none of its own files. Its end state does the same after one edit, and still compares this session and a new one against cold.

**(d) Expired refusals were removed only when their key was asked again** (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`). CONFIRMED: `refusals_for_keys_never_asked_again_are_bounded` (killed by R7).

- Fix: `AnswerCache::hold_degraded`. At `DEGRADED_HELD` (256) it drops the expired refusals, scanning only when the map is full, then the oldest. The map never holds more than the bound.
- Test: 256 held, then one at `DEGRADED_RETRY` leaves exactly 1. 256 fresh ones then hold the bound, the oldest is evicted and the newest stays.

**(e) Comment lines past 120 columns.** CONFIRMED: `types/semantic.rs` `is_degraded` doc was 169 columns. Every comment paragraph holding a line this PR added past 120 characters is re-filled to 120. That covers `dependency_types.rs` (3), `ledger.rs` (2), `ledger/tests.rs`, `semantic_hook.rs` (3), `types/semantic.rs` (2), `instantiate.rs` and `kept.rs`; the last two were touched by earlier rounds of this PR. The one remaining line past 120 is a string literal in `dependency_types/tests.rs`, not a comment.

**Dismissed:**

- The repeated "checker unavailable" warning: dismissed in round 5; each copy is tagged to its own component, and the output dedups identical ones.
- `augmentation_scan` reading a file twice: deliberate, the failed read wins and stands for the load (round 5, item 5, tested). A load that sees two states of a racing file reports it as unreadable, the conservative side.
- `#[non_exhaustive]` on the public structs: 0.x minor is the breaking channel, and adding the attribute is itself breaking. A follow-up with constructors, in its own PR.
- `leave_unasked` marking the whole outcome degraded, so `to_bytes` refuses it: not a regression. Before this PR, a budget run's warning already kept the outcome from being stored. Per-key precision on disk is a follow-up.

import re,sys

def blocks(lines):
    i=0
    while i<len(lines):
        m=re.match(r'^(\s*)(//[/!]?)( |$)',lines[i])
        if not m: i+=1; continue
        ind,mk=m.group(1),m.group(2); j=i
        while j<len(lines):
            m2=re.match(r'^(\s*)(//[/!]?)( |$)',lines[j])
            if not m2 or m2.group(1)!=ind or m2.group(2)!=mk: break
            j+=1
        yield i,j,ind,mk; i=j
def text(lines,i,j,ind,mk):
    return ' '.join(l[len(ind)+len(mk):].strip() for l in lines[i:j])
mode=sys.argv[1]
for f in sys.argv[2:]:
    lines=open(f).read().split('\n')
    out=[];last=0
    for i,j,ind,mk in list(blocks(lines)):
        t=text(lines,i,j,ind,mk)
        if not PAT.search(t): continue
        if mode=='show':
            print(f"--- {f}:{i+1}\n{t}\n")

PAT=re.compile(r'(On the base|on the base|[Bb]efore this (change|PR)|was previously)')
def blocks(lines):
    i=0
    while i<len(lines):
        m=re.match(r'^(\s*)(//[/!]?)( |$)',lines[i])
        if not m: i+=1; continue
        ind,mk=m.group(1),m.group(2); j=i
        while j<len(lines):
            m2=re.match(r'^(\s*)(//[/!]?)( |$)',lines[j])
            if not m2 or m2.group(1)!=ind or m2.group(2)!=mk: break
            j+=1
        yield i,j,ind,mk; i=j
def text(lines,i,j,ind,mk):
    return ' '.join(l[len(ind)+len(mk):].strip() for l in lines[i:j])
mode=sys.argv[1]
for f in sys.argv[2:]:
    lines=open(f).read().split('\n')
    out=[];last=0
    for i,j,ind,mk in list(blocks(lines)):
        t=text(lines,i,j,ind,mk)
        if not PAT.search(t): continue
        if mode=='show':
            print(f"--- {f}:{i+1}\n{t}\n")
EOF

**A checker outage or an unreadable dependency file no longer sticks to a component.** The next request or run asks again and gets the real answer.

- Why it matters: in a watch or Storybook session, one checker timeout, crash or rejected request left the component on its structural props until a source file changed.
- Why it matters: a dependency `.d.ts` that could not be read once (too many open files, an install racing the run) counted as "not exported", for the rest of the session and for later runs.

**What you see now**

- Every answer a checker failure affects carries a warning that says so.
- The checker is asked about the component again 30 seconds after it failed, or after the next source-file change.
- Until then, a request gets the structural props and the warning at once, without waiting on the checker.
- A component the checker skipped because it passed its memory budget is asked again the same way.
- A generic component (`as` props) whose request the checker rejected is asked again instead of being kept without its props.
- A rejected lookup of a component's module says what the checker rejected, instead of "not part of the checker's program".
- A dependency file that cannot be read is reported once in each answer it affects.
- The answer keeps every type the other files gave, including one a later `export *` target declares and a package type's own props.
- Once the file reads, the component has its full props, including a prop a package type inherits from that file, and the warning is gone.
- A file that stays unreadable does not slow the session down, and components that never reach it are not affected.
- A run that cannot read one dependency file still remembers every other package lookup, so the next run is as fast as before.

**Limits**

- A dependency file fixed on disk (a `chmod`, a finished install) is picked up 30 seconds after the failed read or at the next source-file change, not at once.

**Breaking:** for Rust users of `caliper-docgen-core`, `SemanticOutcome` has a new field `unavailable` (set only by `SemanticOutcome::unavailable` for every target and by `SemanticOutcome::leave_unasked` for the keys a run did not ask about; `Unavailable::covers` tells which) and `SemanticFallback` a new field `transient`. A struct literal that names every field no longer compiles: add `unavailable: None` and `transient: false`, or build the outcome with `..Default::default()`. Put two outcomes together with `SemanticOutcome::merge`, which keeps the mark.

A dependency `.d.ts` that could not be read once (too many open files, an install racing the run) used to be kept as "not exported", in the session until it restarted and in the dependency index for later runs.

-- What you see now: every answer the failed checker affects carries its warning. The component is asked again 30 seconds later or after the next source-file change; until then a request gets the structural props and the warning at once, without waiting on a checker that just failed. A run that cannot read a dependency file still warns, and keeps everything it could read: a type a later `export *` target declares, and the React augmentations of the other files. The session's next request and the next run read the file again, and once it reads, the component has its full props and the warning is gone.

-- Also covered: a prop that a package's type inherits from another file of the package that could not be read, and a generic component (`as` props) whose instantiation the checker rejected. Each is asked again on the next request instead of being kept without the prop.
-- A file that stays unreadable is reported once in each answer, however many requests a session makes.

-- A file that stays unreadable (a permission error, a broken install) no longer slows the session down. A component behind it is read again 30 seconds after the failed read or after the next source-file change; until then a request returns the answer it already has, without loading or resolving anything. A dependency file that is fixed on disk is picked up at that retry or edit. Components that never reach the file keep their cached work.
-- A run that cannot read one dependency file still records every other package lookup it completed, so the next run does not walk those again.

-- A component the checker was not asked about because the run passed its memory budget is asked again on the next request, once the 30 seconds pass, instead of keeping its structural props until a file changes.
-- A checker rejection while looking up a component's module now says what the checker rejected, as other rejections do, instead of "not part of the checker's program".

## Round 8

Review of `03589371`: nine items. Each real one has a test that fails on `03589371` or a mutation that a test kills (list below). Files edited beyond the owned set: `crates/core/tests/semantic_join.rs` (item 2: its test asserted the old contract that a stopped checker is asked by the next request).

1. **(refuted) A failed read stamped `edits = 0` by a first load makes the walk due on every request after an edit.** A lazy session does take such a layer: `cold_lazy`'s first load (React's names and the imported modules) ran with `Retry::Always`. Traced and tested: `a_failure_the_first_load_recorded_is_followed_again_once_per_retry_after_edits` (React's types unreadable, three edits, then six requests at one instant) costs `(1, 1)` then `(0, 0)` five times on `03589371` too. The first request after the edits is due because an edit arrived, which is the rule; its retry reads the file again and records the failure with the session's count, so the next requests hold until the retry. No other path gives a lazy session an unsessioned layer (`rebuilt_lazy` starts a new session at 0 edits). Kept as a regression test. The literal is gone anyway (item 5): `cold_lazy` stamps its first load with the session's own `Moment` and `Load`.
2. **(CONFIRMED) `Settled::Stopped` was neither kept nor held, so a checker that stops mid-request was asked by every request.** Test: `Reply::Stops` (the delivery is dropped, not cancelled) added to `a_checker_that_answered_nothing_is_asked_again_only_after_the_retry_or_an_edit`. On `03589371`: five requests asked five times (`left: 5, right: 1`). Fix: the delivery holds a stopped request as a refusal for `DEGRADED_RETRY` with the stopped warning (`stopped_warning`, one constructor for both paths), never in `answers`, never stored. `awaits_checker` stays false (a warning, not the pending info). Inside the window one request, after it the checker is asked again, a recovered checker's answer replaces it, an edit asks again. Sweep: the delivery's `Settled` match has one arm per variant (`Stopped` and `Cancelled` split, no wildcard); `refine`'s `Found` and `Settled` matches have no wildcard either. `semantic_join::a_joined_request_the_checker_drops_says_so_and_is_asked_again_after_an_edit` now asserts the held warning without a second request, then an edit asks again.
3. **(CONFIRMED, cost) Every lazy growth rebuilt the unread-walk graph over the whole chain and keyed every project demand.** The graph was built once per growth, of a new layer each time, so a per-layer cache alone changes nothing. Fix: `DependencyLayer::unread_walks` is a `OnceLock<Arc<UnreadWalks>>`, and a layer whose load changed no ledger entry (a growth that met no unread walk, the common case) takes its parent's `Arc` without building. The demand scan checks a demand's directory against the unread walks' directories before building its key, so files elsewhere allocate nothing. Test: `the_unread_walks_are_built_once_per_layer_that_changed_the_ledger` (one unreadable file, 12 growths, every layer asked twice): 1 build; 13 without the parent reuse (U2), 26 without the cache (U3). `memos_read_in_a_file_whose_demand_reaches_an_unread_walk_do_not_outlive_a_growth` guards the directory set (U4). No Chakra instruction count: Chakra has no unreadable file, so `has_marks` is false and this code returns before any of it runs; the counter is the measurement.
4. **(CONFIRMED) The 30 s interval was defined twice.** Now one `pub(crate) const DEGRADED_RETRY` in `dependency_types/ledger.rs`; `semantic_hook.rs` re-exports it (`pub(crate) use crate::dependency_types::DEGRADED_RETRY`), so the link is the compiler's. `READ_RETRY` is gone. Both sides' tests ask at `DEGRADED_RETRY - 1 ms` (held) and `DEGRADED_RETRY` (asked again) by the one constant. It lives in `dependency_types` because `pipeline` depends on it and not the other way; a crate-level `retry` module would need `crates/core/src/lib.rs`, not in this branch's files.
5. **(CONFIRMED by inspection) `Footprint` held an anonymous `(PathKey, u64, Instant, u64)`.** Now `Footprint(Box<[Unreadable]>)`, `Unreadable { path, read: Stamp }`, `Stamp { moment: Moment, load: Load }`, `Moment { at, edits: Edits }`, with `Edits` and `Load` newtypes (`LoadIds` hands out loads). `Retry::Due(Moment)` and `load_at(.., retry, stamp)`; `footprint_holds(&footprint, Moment)` compares the whole stamp. A transposition of edits and load no longer compiles. The one stamp outside a session is `Stamp::unsessioned()` (batch runs and eager revisions, whose stamps nothing compares).
6. **History comments cut.** Every "On the base ..." sentence in the owned files: `semantic_hook.rs` (4), `pipeline/tests.rs` (1), `revision/lazy.rs` (6), `ledger/tests.rs` (6), `dependency_types/tests.rs` (4), `augmentation_tests.rs` (1), `semantic/src/declared.rs` (2), `lib.rs` (1), `instantiate.rs` (1), `kept.rs` (1); each touched block re-filled to 120. Found in files not owned, left as they are: `crates/core/tests/semantic_hook.rs` (2, in this PR's diff), and on `main` already `crates/core/tests/react_declared_props.rs`, `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs` (2), `on_demand.rs` (3), `checker.rs`, `rpc.rs`, `docs/architecture/serialization-formats.md`.
7. **(refuted) A stale `partial_exports` mapping outlives a later walk that finds nothing.** Not reachable: a load over a layer reuses every file the chain read (`parse_source` consults the parent's `parsed`; a flatten copies them), and the export walk takes the first match in order, continuing past an unreadable or non-answering target. So a later walk of the same `(barrel, name)` finds the same mapping, a new one in a file that now reads, or a complete answer. The newest layer's partial mapping already wins (`chain().find_map`, newest first), and a complete answer in `exports` wins over any partial one. A barrel edited on disk reaches a session only through a rebuild, which starts a new layer. No failing test could be built; no change.
8. **(dismissed) `BatchAnswers` memory and serialization (`asked.rs`).** On `main` already via #513; the measured Chakra memory gate shows no regression. Follow-up.
9. **Changeset rewritten**: one idea per bullet, in the user's words, no internals; "What you see now" split into single-idea bullets, the two 30-second bullets merged, a **Limits** label for the picked-up-at-the-retry behaviour; the `**Breaking:**` paragraph kept.

Mutation proof (`/tmp/claude-501/fix527f/mutate8.py`, each alone): 4 of 5 KILLED.

- KILLED: U1 a stopped checker is not held (2 tests); U2 a layer that changed no ledger entry builds its own walks; U3 the walks are not cached in the layer; U4 the directory set is empty.
- SURVIVED, equivalent: U5, `cold_lazy` stamps its first load `Stamp::unsessioned()`. A new session's moment is 0 edits at the time of the load and its first load id is 0, the same values; the typed stamp is what keeps a later change from mixing them up.

GATES

The Entire reviewer's four findings at `bd8d772c`, each CONFIRMED by a test that fails with its rule set back to `bd8d772c` (mutations V1-V6 below). **(A) A batch over the refusal bound asked a down checker again.** CONFIRMED: `a_batch_larger_than_the_prune_size_repeated_within_the_retry_asks_nothing`. 300 components, the checker down: on `bd8d772c` the first batch asked 300 times and the repeat asked again, since each new refusal evicted the oldest fresh one.

- Fix, both parts asked for. An outcome unavailable for every target (the mark only `SemanticOutcome::unavailable` makes, compared by value) settles as `Settled::Unavailable` and sets one shared `AnswerCache::outage` deadline. Until `DEGRADED_RETRY` passes or an edit, every request without a kept answer is refused with what the checker said, its `affects` set to that component. Per-key refusals (a transient fallback, a stopped checker, a run that left some keys unasked) are pruned by age, not count: once the map reaches `prune_at` (at least `DEGRADED_HELD`), the expired ones go and the next prune waits until the map doubles. A refusal is never dropped before its retry.
- Test: down, 300 components, 1 request, then 0 for the repeat. Rejected (per key): 300, then 0. `refusals_for_keys_never_asked_again_are_bounded` now asserts 257 fresh refusals all kept, then the expired ones go at twice the size. Two integration assertions changed with the contract: a second component during an outage is refused without a request (`semantic_hook::an_unavailable_checker_warns_on_every_answer...`, `semantic_join::an_unavailable_checker_is_reported...`). Every answer still carries its own warning.

**(B) A partial mapping that added nothing else kept the old resolver context.** CONFIRMED: `a_barrel_mapping_to_a_declaration_loaded_directly_reaches_the_resolver`. `D` loads `second.d.ts` through `'barrel-kit/second'`, then `S` (same directory) finds `SecondProps` through the barrel past the unreadable `first.d.ts`. With the rule removed, `S` answered `["own"]`; now `["own", "second"]`, equal to a fresh session over the same unreadable file.

- Fix: `Totals` counts `partial_exports`, and `resolves_like` compares it. A layer keeps only partial mappings that differ from the chain's newest one, so a retry that finds the same mapping again is still no growth (asserted in the same test; V4).

Fix: one function, `touch`, names ids in a delta. `next_lazy` passes the provisional ids through it, and `rebuilt_lazy` passes memo and provisional ids alike. Sweep: those are the only two delta builders that read `previous.memo` (`grep previous.memo`). After the rebuild `A` equals a cold run.

**(D) `typeof Primitive.div` past an unreadable `export *` target lost its props.** CONFIRMED: `component_props_of_a_member_found_past_an_unreadable_star_target_bind_the_key` (Radix's mapped `Primitive` behind `export * from './first'` (unreadable), then `'./prim'`). - Fix: `callee.rs` reads `export_for_resolver`.
- `export_of` is renamed `export_of_complete` and is `#[cfg(test)]`: after this change no non-test code reads complete-only answers. A new caller must pick `export_for_resolver`, or bring the complete-only accessor back by name.
- Callers of the export accessors, each decided: `resolver/import.rs` `follow_reexports` uses `export_for_resolver`, as before. `resolver/callee.rs` `value_member_props_at_depth` now uses `export_for_resolver`. The loader's own lookups (`find_export_in`) use `export_entry`, complete only, since what they cache goes to the index. Tests use `export_of_complete` to assert what the index would write.

Model test: `Direct` (imports `BProps` from `'mk/b'`, the package's module itself) joins the model's components. The model's per-request check (equal to a fresh session over exactly the files it warns about) now covers a declaration loaded directly before or after the barrel walk. It does not kill V3 by itself under its eight seeds; the unit test does. (D)'s qualified `typeof` and (C)'s config rebuild are not in the model: the model has no React types for `ComponentProps`, and no config file to rebuild on.

Mutation proof (`/tmp/claude-501/fix527f/mutate9.py`, each alone): 6 of 6 KILLED. V1 no shared outage deadline; V2 a prune drops fresh refusals; V3 `resolves_like` ignores partial mappings; V4 a partial mapping equal to the chain's counts as a change; V5 the rebuild names only the memo; V6 `callee.rs` reads complete exports only.

## Round 9b

The model test now catches all three round-9 bugs (B, C, D) on `bd8d772c`'s source, and passes at `e379b2f4`. Only `crates/core/src/dependency_types/ledger/tests.rs` changed.

What it lacked, and what was added:

- **A direct importer.** `Direct` imports `BProps` through the stub (`mk/stub`), plus `Missing` and `Nest` from the barrel. Its `Missing` walk resolves every barrel target, so a later barrel walk of `BProps` past an unreadable `a.d.ts` adds only a partial mapping. Importing through `mk/b` (round 9) did not reach the bug: the barrel walk then cached the stub's own export, which changed the counts.
- **A qualified `typeof X.y` consumer.** `Q` is `ComponentProps<typeof Primitive.div>`, with Radix's mapped `Primitive` behind the barrel's last `export *`.
- **A config edit event.** The project has a `tsconfig.json`; the event rewrites it with the same meaning, and the session takes its rebuild path. It is checked like a project edit: every component whose answer changed must be in the delta.
- **A second oracle that shares no failed-read code.** The props must equal a fresh session's with the warned files declaring nothing (`export {};`). The first oracle (a fresh session over the same unreadable files) runs the code under test, so it could not see D, which a cold run has too.
- **A targeted order enumeration.** Every ordered pair of requests under each single unreadable file, then the file reads and a config edit (9 files x 6 x 5 = 270 sessions), next to the eight random seeds. Each seed's events now include config edits.
- **Every failure is collected** with its rule, seed or pair, and the steps so far, then asserted at once.

Demonstration: a scratch tree at `/tmp/claude-501/fix527f/basewt` (not committed). It is `git archive` of `99c4eb0f` with `bd8d772c`'s `dependency_types.rs`, `semantic_hook.rs`, `resolver/callee.rs` and `revision/lazy.rs`, the new `ledger/tests.rs`, and `export_of_complete` renamed back to `export_of` in the tests. The model test FAILS there with 463 failures:

- B (`resolves_like` without partial mappings): `[fresh session]`, `[readable files]` and `[asked again]` on `pair a: Direct, B`. Only this request order reaches it; no seed does, which is why the enumeration exists.
- C (rebuild delta from the memo only): `[delta]` 421 times, on seeds 1, 2, 3, 5, 21 and 34 and on most pairs.

"""Re-fill to 120 columns every comment block holding a line over 120 characters. 'show' prints them instead."""
import re
import sys
import textwrap

LINE = re.compile(r'^(\s*)(//[/!]?)( |$)')
mode, files = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]
for f in files:
    lines = open(f).read().split('\n')
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(lines):
        m = LINE.match(lines[i])
        if not m:
            out.append(lines[i])
            i += 1
            continue
        ind, mk = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        j = i
        while j < len(lines) and (m2 := LINE.match(lines[j])) and m2.group(1) == ind and m2.group(2) == mk:
            j += 1
        block = lines[i:j]
        if not any(len(line) > 120 for line in block):
            out.extend(block)
            i = j
            continue
        if mode == 'show':
            print(f'--- {f}:{i + 1}')
            print('\n'.join(block))
            out.extend(block)
            i = j
            continue
        # Paragraphs split at blank comment lines; a list item starts its own paragraph and keeps a hanging indent.
        paras, cur = [], []
        for line in block:
            body = line[len(ind) + len(mk):]
            text = body.strip()
            if text == '':
                paras.append(cur)
                paras.append(None)
                cur = []
            elif re.match(r'(- |\* |\d+\. )', text):
                paras.append(cur)
                cur = [text]
            else:
                cur.append(text)
        paras.append(cur)
        for para in paras:
            if para is None:
                out.append(ind + mk)
                continue
            if not para:
                continue
            text = ' '.join(para)
            item = re.match(r'(- |\* |\d+\. )', text)
            hang = ' ' * len(item.group(1)) if item else ''
            width = 120 - len(ind) - len(mk) - 1
            wrapped = textwrap.wrap(text, width, subsequent_indent=hang, break_long_words=False, break_on_hyphens=False)
            out.extend(ind + mk + ' ' + w for w in wrapped)
        i = j
    if mode == 'fix':
        open(f, 'w').write('\n'.join(out))
